title: RIFT six-copy common-Z spaghetti failure under C02-style motion
finding: A six-copy RIFT plate using one identical STL remained adhered to the bed but developed a repeatable horizontal disturbance at a common Z across multiple copies, followed by localized loose extrusion and cross-object spaghetti. The exact failed job used the custom process 'RIFT 0.20mm - Original Body Motion - Upper Closure Check', which resolves to C02-style aggressive motion (300 mm/s inner wall, 200 mm/s outer wall, 250 mm/s gap infill, 10000 mm/s^2 default acceleration, 5000 mm/s^2 outer-wall acceleration, 10000 mm/s^2 travel acceleration, reduce-crossing-walls off). Height Slowdown is enabled only from 120-132 mm and occurs above the observed onset, so it is not considered the initiating cause. Current leading hypothesis: repeatable geometry/toolpath interaction amplified by the aggressive motion envelope, producing local lift/curl or part deflection and subsequent nozzle contact. Filament/bed adhesion are lower-probability primary causes because all six copies stayed attached and the unaffected walls remained largely uniform.

reference_context.reserved_followup: E-024 remains reserved for the v51/Kexcelled terracotta follow-up declared by E-023; this unplanned RIFT failure is intentionally tested by E-025.

event.source_relationship: all six plate objects are copies of the same STL
event.stop_reason: Bambu spaghetti detection; visual inspection confirmed a true-positive localized extrusion failure
event.failure_pattern: common horizontal disturbance at approximately the same Z across multiple identical copies, with loose filament subsequently dragged between objects
physical_notes: All six bodies remained standing and adhered to their brims/plate at inspection.
Large flat wall regions above and below the disturbed band remained comparatively uniform.
Failure was concentrated near repeated side/end geometry rather than distributed across every wall surface.

resolved_process.name: RIFT 0.20mm - Original Body Motion - Upper Closure Check

height_slowdown.assessment: retained for now; begins above the observed failure onset and is not the leading initiating mechanism

resolved_filament.name: SUNLU PLA Grey - Reliable
resolved_filament.assessment: no strong evidence that filament settings initiated the failure; leave unchanged for the first diagnostic rerun

evidence.photo_storage: Photos were supplied in the 2026-10-29 ChatGPT failure-review session. The hashes above bind this case to those exact originals; binary photo files are not yet copied into the Git repository.
evidence.artifact_storage: The failed-job artifacts are hash-bound above. The replacement diagnostic project and presets are now stored in the repository and linked through E-025.

hypotheses.cause: repeatable geometry/toolpath interaction amplified by excessive wall speed/acceleration for tall narrow parts
local raised/curling extrusion or part deflection leading to nozzle contact

next_test.intent: isolate motion sensitivity without changing filament, temperatures, geometry, or the 120-132 mm Height Slowdown
next_test.decision_rule: If the one-copy rerun clears the common-Z failure region without wall disturbance or nozzle contact, motion sensitivity becomes the primary supported mechanism. If it fails at the same geometry/Z despite the reduced motion envelope, inspect the exact local geometry/toolpath transition before any further global tuning.
